newsitem.title: CHINA: HONG KONG STOCKS SEEN CORRECTING AFTER RECORD RUN.
newsitem.headline: HONG KONG STOCKS SEEN CORRECTING AFTER RECORD RUN.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to come under some selling pressure on Friday, but brokers said downside should be limited.
"I expect to see some profit-taking in blue chips today," said a broker with a large local house, adding the sell-off in both first-tier stocks and China plays late Thursday was quite radical.

The Hang Seng Index set a second consecutive record close on Thursday of 16,673.27 after soaring to an all-time high of 16,820.31 on record turnover of HK$34.20 billion. The index has set new records in six of the past seven trading days.
"We have had a good rally over the week and I think we will see the market correct about 200 points or so," said a trader with a U.S. brokerage.
Reasons for the correction were pre-weekend caution, a follow-through of the selling seen late Thursday afternoon and external factors, brokers said.
"The bond market is worse and the Dow corrected last night," said the U.S. trader. "This should weigh on the market a bit."
The Dow dropped 71.31 points to close at 8,188.00 and the U.S. 30-year bond closed at 101-8/32, down 20/32 to yield 6.53 percent, the first close above 6.50 percent since July 21.
